subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

Learn to **separate what is useful from what is worthless**. Otherwise, you will always be tied up with unnecessary things.

options.text: Let the cat out of the bag
Separate the wheat from the chaff

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Separate the wheat from the chaff"** means to distinguish valuable or useful things from worthless ones. (अनाज को भूसे से अलग करना)

 
 
• **Example: **It's important to separate the wheat from the chaff when reading articles online.
 
 
 
• **Separate the wheat from the chaff** refers to the process of sorting out the valuable from the worthless or unimportant. (अनाज को भूसे से अलग करना)
 
 
• **Example: **During the interview process, it's crucial to separate the wheat from the chaff to find the best candidates.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Let the cat out of the bag** (बिल्ली को थैले से बाहर निकालना): To reveal a secret or disclose information unintentionally.

 
 
• **Example:** She let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Spill the beans** (राज़ खोल देना): To reveal secret information or divulge something confidential.
 
 
• **Example: **He spilled the beans about their engagement before they could announce it.
 
 
 
• **Chew the cud** (जुगाली करना): To think carefully about something over a period of time.
 
 
• **Example:** He sat quietly, chewing the cud over the decision he had to make.
 
 

 

3b:Tc51,
The correct answer is **Option 4**.
